characters.name: King Arthur
characters.description: A handsome and carefree young man, who finds himself thrown into conflict when Merlin arrives and reveals he's the son of King Uther. Adaptational Jerkass: Arthur feels little guilt for sleeping with a woman Kay had been courting while later having an affair with Guinevere, despite her being engaged to Leontes who saved Arthur's life. Though he does acknowledge that he's harmed Leontes once he's discovered the affair and is willing to claim that he pressured Guinevere into sleeping with him. Bed Trick:Morgana disguises herself as Guinevere to conceive a child with Arthur. Betty and Veronica: The edgy Veronica to Leontes' Betty. Broken Pedestal: In "The Battle of Bardon Pass" his affair with Guinevere is exposed and all his men are disappointed and angered by this. He also loses the faith of the people because of Morgan's manipulations.

characters.name: Merlin
characters.description: A mysterious court sorcerer who seeks to make Arthur king. Adaptational Relationship Overhaul: Merlin and Igraine never really interacted in the Legend, while here the two converse often and even haveUnresolved Sexual Tension. Adaptational Sexuality:Word of Gayconfirms that Merlin is meant to be bisexual, while his Legend counterpart only showed interest in women. Thoughthe same is true for this versionas well. Addictive Magic: Merlin views his powers as this, accusing it of taking too high a price on his body and harming people around him. The Ageless: Igraine notes that he hasn't aged a day since Arthur's birth and Arthur suspects he planted the Sword of Mars into the cliff centuries ago.

characters.name: Guinevere
characters.description: The wife of Leontes who starts an affair with Arthur. Childhood Friend Romance: Leontes and Guinevere are childhood sweethearts and have been betrothed for the last five years. Consummation Counterfeit: Guinevere puts some pig's blood on her bedsheets after her wedding night with Leontes, worried he would know she lost her virginity to Arthur otherwise. Girl of My Dreams: Arthur dreams of her shortly before meeting her. Love Triangle: Guinevere, Arthur and her betrothed, laterhusbandLeontes.

characters.name: Kay
characters.description: Arthur's adopted older brother who becomes the king's Marsha after Arthur is crowned. Big Brother Instinct: Despite some issues with Arthur, he loves him completely and is fiercely loyal. However he's angered when he discovers that Arthur had an affair with Guinevere, feeling disappointed that his brother failed to be a worthy king. Demoted to Extra: Initially he was a fairly important character and "Three Journeys" does focus on a bit on his family, but he quickly becomes less important to the narrative as the series focuses on characters like Leontes Sybil.

characters.name: Gawain
characters.description: A former knight who is recruited to train Arthur's army. Age Lift: He appears to be several years older than Arthur. Child by Rape: Implied, since he claims that his mother knew what it was like to be raped but doesn't explain the context. Unrelated in the Adaptation: He's not the nephew of Arthur or the son of Lot in this version.

characters.name: Leontes
characters.description: A knight who followed Merlin and is loyal to Arthur, unaware that the king is having an affair with his wife Guinevere. Betty and Veronica: The virtuous Betty to Arthur's bad boy Veronica. Canon Foreigner: There is no knight named Leontes in the myths. Childhood Friend Romance: Leontes and Guinevere are childhood sweethearts and have been betrothed for the last five years. Love Triangle: Leontes is unknowingly in one with his betrothed, and later wife, Guinevere and his new king Arthur.

characters.name: Igraine
characters.description: The mother of Arthur and widow to King Uther. Adaptational Relationship Overhaul: Her and Merlin never really interacted in the Legend, while here the two converse often and even haveUnresolved Sexual Tension. Accomplice by Inaction: Morgan views Igraine as this to Uther's abuse. She's not entirely wrong, but given the kind of man Uther was, there's not much that Igraine could have done. Ascended Extra: Igraine has a far more prominent role in the series unlike in the medieval texts and most other adaptations where she disappears after Arthur's birth. Here she becomes theTeam Momto the Camelot crew and has a romantic subplot with Merlin. Create Your Own Villain:It turns out that it was Igraine, not Uther, who sent Morgan to the nunnery in order to save her life. Except this only led Morgan to become vengeful towards both her and her father.

characters.name: Morgan Pendragon
characters.description: The daughter of King Uther, who poisons him in order to take the throne only to discover her claim challenged by Arthur and Merlin. Adaptational Name Change: FromMorgan le Fayto Morgan Pendragon. Though Arthur strips her of the name Pendragon after discovering her treachery, suggesting that she might have taken the name le Fay if the show wasn't cancelled. Adaptational Sympathy: Morgan le Fay once again gets this treatment here, though only to a certain extent as she's still firmly the villain. Morgan was abused and all but disowned by her father Uther; after he murdered her mother to marry Igraine - who did little to intervene in the abuse - Morgan was sent away to a convent. When she returns to reconcile with Uther, he brutally rejects her, so she poisons him to finally claim the throne she believes is hers by right. Then at her moment of triumph she finds out she has a secret illegitimate half-brother and he’s ahead of her in the succession purely because Merlin thinks he should be. Ambition Is Evil: Morgan wants the throne more than anything and is unable to accept Arthur being ruler, and is willing to send men to attack innocents to make Arthur seem like a weak ruler and gain their support. And Then What?: Sybil is able to reveal through some questions that Morgan actually has no plans beyond being ruler after she has killed Arthur. Her advice helps Morgan realise that if she wants to keep her throne, she needs to ensure the loyalty of the people and improve her public image.

characters.name: Vivian
characters.description: A young woman descended from Roman slaves and becomes a servant for Morgan. Black Vikings: Vivian, Morgan's servant, is black. However, Vivian tells Morgan her ancestors were brought over as slaves from Africa by the Romans, which is actually possible, as some British archaeological findings show that people of African descent (both free and slaves)really did come from Roman Africa to Roman Britain. This could also explain Sir Ulfius, Arthur'sblack knight, though the show doesn't acknowledge he is black as it does with Vivian. Decomposite Character: Her name has been used for the Lady of the Lake in some versions, but here that role is taken by Excalibur and Vivian has nothing in common with the Lady. In Name Only: Has nothing in common with the Lady of the Lake. Pet the Dog: Despite being loyal to Morgan, shechooses to not report that Igraine is escaping when she has the chance.

characters.name: Sybil
characters.description: The nun who raised Morgan and comes to join her at Castle Pendragon. Adaptational Job Change: Sister Sybil, a nun and Morgan's mentor in sorcery, is named after a lady or queen of the same name (with various other old spellings like Sebile or Sedile), anAmbiguously Humannoblewoman/fay enchantress figure akin to Morgan le Fay herself in some medieval legends. Sebile was seemingly inspired by the seeresses called Sybils of classical mythology and hadExpy Coexistencewith Morgan for a while until she fell out of use. While some versions of the legends have Morgan learning magic at a nunnery, the show gives a face to those nuns through Sister Sybil. The medieval Sebile was also younger and the junior to Morgan, while in the show it's reversed with Sibyl being the senior. Dark and Troubled Past:It turns out she left the nunnery after starting a fire to hide the rituals being committed on young girls, seemingly which helps them access magical powers, when the church began investigating. This caused the death of a girl and her mother being burned, making her flee to Morgan. Evil Counterpart: She's a mentor towards Morgan who seeks to aid her in becoming queen, just like Merlin is for Arthur. Merlin actually seems to recognise this and notes that he could grow to like her. Light Is Not Good: Sybil is a nun. Yet she has done some nasty things in past and present.

characters.name: King Uther
characters.description: The father of Morgan and Arthur, who is killed by his daughter. Abusive Parent: The first scene Uther appears in has him hitting Morgan. He was also responsible for banishing Morgan to a nunnery, killing her mother, and overall treated her like garbage when she returned. Asshole Victim: He's such a cruel, selfish, vile man that it's impossible to feel bad for him when Morgan arranges his death. I Have No Daughter!: He has this attitude towards Morgan; it gets him killed.

characters.name: Sir Ector
characters.description: The adopted father of Arthur and biological father of Kay. Death by Adaptation: He's fatally wounded before he kills Lot, while the Legend version is never confirmed to have died (though presumably he would have passed away).

characters.name: King Lot
characters.description: A rival king of Uther who allies with Morgan. Adaptational Relationship Overhaul: Lot is usually the husband of Morguase, or sometimes Morgan, while here they only have a brief alliance before his death.

characters.name: Excalibur
characters.description: The daughter of legendary blacksmith Caliburn. Adaptational Name Change: The Lady of the Lake has never been named Excalibur. Adaptational Wimp: Instead of a sorceress, she's just a normal woman. Aerith and Bob: In this series, Excalibur is a girl's name. Decomposite Character: While her father made the sword, she is the basis for the story of the Lady of the Lake, which Merlin made to cover up her death which was caused by him. Meanwhile the name Vivian is used by a completely unrelated character.
